survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive results and proficiency-level shares for Thailand using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each country. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. Analysts using the PISA microdata should follow the OECD PISA technical documentation (Reader’s Guide and annexes referenced in the note) to apply the appropriate student sampling weights and replicate-weight procedures when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Thailand factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Thailand performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean-score trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2 and Level 5/6), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, bullying, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. For Thailand, 8,495 students in 279 schools completed the assessment in 2022, and the note states that all data met PISA quality standards. The factsheet also explains the PISA assessment structure (two 2-hour subject tests with rotated booklets and a background questionnaire) and provides OECD table references for the reported estimates. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an ML study, no predictive model performance metrics or algorithmic methods are evaluated here.
